coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia team-season page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Florida_Gators_football_team — has an explicit "Coaching staff" section listing all 10 on-field coaches; every quote I cite from it was mechanically verified present in the rendered page text. (2) The school's own archived staff directory: https://web.archive.org/web/20081007232739/http://www.gatorzone.com/football/bios/roster/spring2008coaches.html — a snapshot taken 7 Oct 2008, i.e. DURING the championship season, titled "2008 Coaches". This is the strongest source and independently confirms all 10 on-field coaches with the school's own wording. Also used the 9 Aug 2008 snapshot of gatorzone.com/football/bios.php?year=2008, which additionally lists Terry Jackson under a "Staff" heading. (3) The 2008 Florida Football Media Guide PDF (archived copy, ~115 MB, 208 pp.): https://web.archive.org/web/20200904105537/https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/gatorzone.com/documents/2016/2/11/2008_FB_media_guide.pdf — pp. 88-92 carry the full support-staff bios and photo grid, p. 22 the "2008 Sports Health Staff" panel, p. 205 a "Staff Information" quick-facts block. This is where essentially all non-on-field staff came from.

WHY MANY QUOTES ARE EMPTY. Everything sourced only to the media guide has quote: "". That PDF's text layer does not extract faithfully — it renders letter-spaced/justified display type, so extraction produces artifacts like "P atriots", "Ky l e  J o h n s t o n", "or thopaedic", "UF ,". A verbatim string match would fail through no fault of the claim. I instead rendered each relevant page to an image and read it visually, and put the exact printed name and title plus page number in each source note. So those rows are real and eyeball-verified, just not string-matchable. The 11 rows sourced to Wikipedia and to GatorZone HTML do carry true verbatim quotes, all of which I programmatically confirmed match the live page text.

WEB SEARCH WAS UNAVAILABLE. This session's web-search budget was exhausted before I started, so I could not run contemporary-news sweeps (hire announcements, championship-week coverage). Everything here came from direct URL fetches and the Wayback CDX index. That mainly cost me the ability to chase mid-season personnel churn and to confirm titles against news reporting.

TIER-BY-TIER HONESTY.
- Head coach and on-field assistants (10 of 10): COMPLETE and double-sourced. Florida ran the full NCAA-allowed 9 assistants plus Meyer.
- Strength and conditioning (4): believed complete for football — Marotti, Holsopple, Campbell, Piraino. Only Marotti and Holsopple also appear in the p. 205 quick-facts block; Campbell and Piraino come from their p. 89/91 bios.
- Graduate assistants (2): Sean Cronin (defense) and Zach Smith (offense) are the only two given bios. Programs of this era were capped at two football GAs, so this is very likely complete, but I could not affirmatively rule out unlisted GAs.
- ANALYSTS AND QUALITY CONTROL: RECOVERED ZERO, and I believe that is correct rather than a gap. No one on the 2008 staff carries an "analyst" or "quality control" title anywhere in the media guide. The only QC reference is retrospective — Zach Smith's bio noting he "took the role as a Special Teams and Offensive Quality Control assistant" in 2006, a job he had left by 2008. The large off-field analyst rooms of the modern era did not exist under 2008 NCAA staff limits. I have returned no analyst or qc rows; do not read that as thin documentation.
- Operations / personnel / recruiting (9): good coverage, though two people carry conflicting titles between the bio pages and the p. 205 quick-facts block (Jon Clark: "Director of Football Operations" vs "Director of Football Administration"; Nancy Scarborough: "Executive Assistant to Head Coach" vs "Office Manager"). I used the bio-page wording and flagged the variant in each note.
- Equipment (2), medical/sports health (25 including student trainers), and student managers (10): documented, but with the caveat below.

TWO CAVEATS THAT AFFECT RING ELIGIBILITY.
- TIMING. The media guide went to press in mid-June 2008 (page footers read 6/14/08 and 6/15/08), before the season began. The GatorZone coaches page I used is from 7 Oct 2008, mid-season, and matches the guide exactly for on-field coaches — so the coaching staff was demonstrably stable. For the support tiers I have no January 2009 snapshot and therefore cannot prove each person was still on staff at the BCS title game on 8 Jan 2009. I found no evidence of any support-staff departure, but that is absence of evidence.
- SCOPE. Some medical, nutrition, and dental personnel (Chris Patrick, Jay Clugston, Tim Shay, Susan Tillman, Anna Grout, Cheryl Zonkowski, and the oral surgeons/dentist/ophthalmologist) are University Athletic Association department-wide staff who appear in the football guide and serve football, not football-only employees. Likewise the six athletic training students and ten student managers are students, not staff hires. I included them because they are documented on the team's staff pages, but you may want to gate them out of ring counts. They are all flagged in their notes.

ONE MID-SEASON NOTE. Dan Mullen was hired as Mississippi State's head coach on 11 December 2008 but remained Florida's offensive coordinator through the 8 January 2009 title game, so he satisfies the ring rule. Flagged on his row. The three 2008 departures Wikipedia mentions in "Before the season" — Doc Holliday to West Virginia, Stan Drayton to Tennessee, Greg Mattison to the Ravens — all left BEFORE the 2008 season and are deliberately excluded; Bedford, Carter and McCarney are their replacements. No names in this dataset are inferred or padded.
